description: 11 branding agencies for startups, from Bolder, The Branx and Second Eight to Pentagram, with locations, prices, timelines, past work and contact details.
body:
For a startup, a strong brand identity is not just nice to have.

It helps investors, customers and new hires understand what you do before they have time to read the details.

That matters most right before a round, which is why I wrote a separate guide on why you need branding before you raise.

I’ve refreshed this list for 2026, comparing agency websites and available directories for location, pricing, timeline, past work and contact details.

The list runs from startup-focused studios to some of the world’s best-known firms, and ends with my own practice as a solo alternative, so you can compare them by budget and stage.

What is the best branding agency for a startup?

The best fit depends on the job, budget and stage of your startup.

For a technical early-stage company, Bolder and The Branx are worth comparing for their stated startup focus and the pricing information available below.

For a science, health or AI startup that wants one senior designer leading the identity, motion and website, look at Second Eight.

For a digital product that needs brand and interface design, look at Ramotion and Clay; for a larger positioning and rollout challenge, consider a firm such as Motto or Further.

If you need a focused identity and direct access to the designer, my own practice, Ebaq Design, is a solo alternative starting at $3,000 for one week.

These are editorial recommendations based on stated services and examples of work, not an independently tested ranking or a guarantee that any firm is available or right for your project.

I include my own practice, so I have a commercial interest in one of the options; compare the work, references and proposals before deciding.

Which branding partner fits your startup stage?

Start with the decision you need to make before launch, then use scope, budget and proof of similar work to narrow the shortlist.

Pre-seed: Launch with an identity your team can use

If your positioning is clear and the immediate need is a logo, visual system and guidelines, compare a focused identity engagement with a broader agency proposal.

Ebaq Design’s Brand Sprint is $3,000 for one week; its Periti case study shows how the identity extends beyond the logo.

If the buyer, positioning or name is still undecided, ask for discovery and strategy as separate deliverables before booking a visual sprint.

Seed: Make a technical product easier to explain

When you need a brand and a marketing site to explain an unfamiliar product, compare teams that show how they carried the same story across both.

Bolder lists early-stage projects from $15,000 and shows deep-tech work for Acorn Biolabs and Alicia.

The Branx focuses on AI and SaaS, with examples such as Dablam and Metricool; request a current quote for the identity and website scope.

Second Eight designs identities, motion and websites for science, health and AI startups, with examples such as Aikka.ai and Sixfold.

For a solo-led example of identity and website work, see Ebaq Design’s NextDimension AI redesign.

Series A and beyond: Plan for the rollout

If the rebrand needs to reach an existing customer base, multiple product teams or sales channels, budget for research, messaging, rollout and handoff alongside the new identity.

Bolder’s contact FAQ lists $35,000–$200,000 for Series A-to-IPO work, as one agency’s reference point.

Ask shortlisted teams for a relevant rebrand case study and a proposal that names the rollout deliverables, owners and milestones.

1. Bolder

Bolder describes itself as the agency that brands “the companies that are hardest to explain.”

Bolder work page. Image source.

It focuses on AI, robotics, biotech, energy and deep tech, where the product is often harder to explain than to build.

The work page opens with a 3D render of the Alicia robot, labeled with real specs like torque and cleaning area.

I like that approach, because it turns technical detail into the visual language instead of hiding it.

The Acorn biotech identity takes another route, with wide monospaced type over a textured, microscope-like surface.

Bolder also publishes its prices, which is rare: pre-seed and seed projects start at $15,000 and take two to eight weeks.

Location: San Francisco, New York, Berlin and London
Timeline: 2–8 weeks for pre-seed and seed; 6–16 weeks for Series A and later
Price: From $15,000 for early-stage branding and websites; $35,000–$200,000 for Series A to IPO
Past work: Alicia, Acorn Biolabs, Attero, Brightly
Contact: Project form; they reply within 24 hours

View Bolder’s work.

Read Bolder’s client reviews on Clutch.

2. The Branx

The Branx calls itself the tech branding agency for AI and SaaS startups.

The Branx work page. Image source.

The Branx says it has built more than 120 tech brands across the US, Canada, the UK and Europe.

Its portfolio is clean and product-led, with marks that work well as app icons and on dark interfaces.

I like the Dablam symbol, a circle cut by vertical strokes, set against a glowing mountain ridge.

The Eluviant wordmark is another strong example: stacked horizontal lines suggest motion and video without any literal camera icon.

The Branx describes a three-week branding process; ask the team to confirm timing and scope for your project.

Location: Spain (The Branx Europe S.L.); works across the US, Canada, the UK and the EU
Timeline: About 3 weeks for the process described on its site; confirm for your scope
Price: Request a quote; Clutch lists a $25,000+ minimum, but also shows a $20,000 package
Past work: Metricool, Furanova, Dablam, Eluviant, Featherless, North, docStribute, Causaly
Contact: hi@thebranx.com or the project form

View The Branx’s work.

Read The Branx’s client reviews on Clutch.

3. Second Eight

Second Eight is a branding agency for science, health and technology startups, founded by Sam Hox.

Second Eight homepage. Image source.

It works with startups from pre-seed to Series A on naming, identity, motion, pitch decks and websites.

It is a small studio by design: Sam leads and designs every project, takes two clients at a time and brings in collaborators for animation or development.

I like how the work makes science visual without clichés: the Sixfold project glows like a blue microscope scan, and Cellbased is a white cellular sphere rather than a stock DNA helix.

The process starts with research into your science and market, then two or three directions, one of which is built into the full system.

Clients receive full rights and all source files at handover, and its marks have appeared on the cover of LogoLounge Book 12.

Location: Europe and New York; works with clients in the US and Europe
Timeline: A few weeks for most identity projects; agreed before work starts
Price: A weekly rate, with the number of weeks agreed before work starts
Past work: Aikka.ai, Sixfold, Radial, Gray Matter, Cultiv, Cellbased, Tessel, Bad Decisions Studio
Contact: contact@secondeight.net or the contact form; they reply within one working day

View Second Eight’s work.

4. Ramotion

Ramotion is a brand and digital product agency with offices in San Francisco, Los Angeles and New York.

Ramotion work page. Image source.

It runs dedicated programs for startups, with branding, web design and UX under one roof.

Its work page includes Firefox, Salesforce, Stripe, Netflix and Descript; the type of work varies by project, so check each case study before comparing.

I like how the Firefox posters use bright gradients and bold slogans to make privacy feel energetic rather than technical.

That mix of brand and product design is useful for startups whose app is the brand.

Pricing isn’t published, so expect to discuss budget on a first call.

Location: 28 Geary St, San Francisco; also Los Angeles and New York
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Firefox, Salesforce, Clearbit, Turo, Netflix, Citrix, Descript, Stripe, Volusion, Okta
Contact: newbusiness@ramotion.com or +1 415 831 7880

View Ramotion’s work.

Read Ramotion’s client reviews on Clutch.

5. Wolff Olins

Wolff Olins is a global brand consultancy that works “from global icons to trailblazing start-ups.”

Wolff Olins work page. Image source.

It is best known for big identities like Uber, TikTok and Lloyds, but its recent work also includes fast-growing challengers.

The Blank Street coffee identity is a good example, with a bright green, hand-painted-style sign that feels local despite rapid expansion.

Patreon’s shift from membership model to creator company is another startup-to-scale-up story in the portfolio.

I would consider Wolff Olins for a well-funded company at a defining moment, such as a major raise or category change.

Earlier versions of this article mentioned a dedicated startup division, but I couldn’t find one on its current site.

Location: London, New York, San Francisco and Los Angeles
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; request a quote
Past work: Blank Street, Patreon, Decathlon, Benefit, Lloyds, Hyundai Card, LG, TikTok, Uber
Contact: clientsnewyork@wolffolins.com or clientslondon@wolffolins.com

View Wolff Olins’s work.

6. Pentagram

Pentagram is one of the world’s best-known design firms, run by independent partners in New York, London, Austin and Berlin.

Pentagram work page. Image source.

Its motto is “we design everything for everyone,” and the work covers technology and finance as well as arts and culture.

The latest projects show its typographic range: the BFI London Film Festival identity, a 40th-anniversary mark for MTA Arts & Design and the Storefront Gala.

I like how each identity is built around one strong typographic idea rather than a generic symbol.

For a startup, the advantage is working directly with a senior partner and their team.

The trade-off is budget, so Pentagram suits founders who see the identity as a long-term asset.

Location: 250 Park Avenue South, New York; also London, Austin and Berlin
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: BFI London Film Festival, MTA Arts & Design, Storefront for Art and Architecture
Contact: newyork@pentagram.com or +1 212 683 7000

View Pentagram’s work.

7. Motto

Motto is a strategic branding agency for technology and innovation companies at defining moments of growth.

Archival screenshot of Motto’s website. Image source.

It is best known for its “Ideas Worth Rallying Around” approach, which puts purpose and positioning before visuals.

Its listed clients include Microsoft, Google, Disney, Andela, Goodnotes, Prolific and Klaviyo.

That makes Motto a strong fit for startups whose biggest problem is the story, not the logo.

Clutch lists a minimum project size of $100,000, so it is best for well-funded teams.

Motto’s website blocks automated visits, so the image above is from an earlier capture.

Location: New York, London, Berlin and Dallas
Timeline: Motto’s FAQ says at least 16 weeks for a fast-track startup project and at least 6–8 months for comprehensive branding
Price: Minimum project size of $100,000+ (Clutch)
Past work: Microsoft, Google, Disney, Andela, Goodnotes, Prolific, Klaviyo
Contact: Contact form on Motto’s website

8. Mucho

Mucho is an independent design studio with offices in San Francisco and Barcelona.

Mucho work page. Image source.

It works across strategy, brand identity, websites, packaging and environments.

The portfolio mixes cultural clients like MACBA with startups such as Biotic and Eko Health.

I like the Biotic identity, where a dense dotted circle suggests a biological process without a literal leaf or cell.

Mucho’s strength is craft and range, from bold editorial type to playful packaging like Baby Bites.

That makes it a good fit for consumer and health startups that need a brand to work in print and in person, not just on screens.

Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Biotic, Eko Health, Alianza, MACBA, Art Gallery of NSW, Baby Bites, Krateo Sky

9. Clay

Clay is a remote-first UX design and branding agency headquartered in San Francisco.

Clay work page. Image source.

It is strongest in digital product and web design, with clients including Meta, Google, Stripe and Coinbase.

Earlier versions of this article credited Clay with Snapchat and Slack branding, but its site describes that work as UX design for Snapchat and web design for Slack.

Its brand identities are still worth a look, like the bold radiating gradient for the DeFi platform Sky.

I would choose Clay for a startup whose product experience matters as much as its logo.

Location: San Francisco; also New York, Austin, Denver, Lisbon and Belgrade
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Meta, Google, Slack (web), Snapchat (UX), Coinbase, Stripe, Discover, Credit Karma, Marqeta, Sky
Contact: hey@clay.global or +1 415 796 6262

10. Further (formerly DesignStudio)

Further is the new name of DesignStudio, the agency behind the famous Airbnb rebrand.

Further work page. Image source.

It still has a collection called “Branding Unicorns”, featuring Airbnb, Deliveroo and GetYourGuide.

The newer work is just as bold, from the Wimbledon identity to a high-energy look for rugby’s HSBC SVNS series.

I like the Eurostar rebrand in particular, where a star-like spark becomes a livery graphic across the whole train.

Further is a good fit for startups preparing for a global launch or IPO, where the brand has to work at a very large scale.

Location: London (12–16 Clerkenwell Road), New York (300 Kent Avenue, Brooklyn) and Dubai
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Airbnb, Deliveroo, GetYourGuide, Eurostar, Wimbledon, Depop, EA Sports, HSBC SVNS
Contact: newyork@further.group or london@further.group

View Further’s work.

11. Ebaqdesign

Ebaqdesign is my own practice in New York, and it isn’t a typical multi-person agency: I work as a solo branding expert, so founders deal with the senior designer directly, not an account team.

Ebaqdesign homepage. Image source.

I’m Arek Dvornechuck, a Branding Expert with over 20 years of experience.

Before starting my own practice, I worked with leading design firms, including Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv.

Most startups I work with need to look established before a raise, a launch or their first enterprise sale.

A scoped brand identity or rebrand starts at one week for $3,000: logo system, colors, typography and practical guidelines.

Larger scopes, such as a website, motion or a full brand system, take extra weeks at the same weekly rate.

For recent examples, see Periti Digital, Savory and the Airport Executive rebrand.

You can also read client feedback on my Clutch profile and Contra reviews.

These are sources to check alongside the actual work and a conversation about your project; neither listing proves that I am the right fit for every startup.

Location: New York City; solo branding expert working with clients worldwide
Timeline: 1 week+ (one week for a scoped identity; more weeks for larger scopes)
Price: $3,000 per week
Past work: Periti Digital, Savory, Airport Executive, Orbio, NextDim AI, Elevate, Lyntics
Contact: Book a call

Discuss your startup brand with Arek.

Choosing the right agency for your startup

When you compare agencies, I would look at five things.

Read the full case study and the full review.

Look for the project’s original problem, the work the agency actually led, and examples applied beyond a single mockup.

For a branding and website project, ask to see the identity across real pages and find out who handled design, development, content, and launch.

Use referrals, agency portfolios, and review directories to build a shortlist, then use the same brief and questions with each candidate.

Directories can help you find client feedback, but a listing or placement is not proof that a team fits your budget or brief.

Clutch explains how it ranks providers and displays sponsored listings in its directory methodology.

  1. Portfolio alignment: look for work in your industry, or at least for companies at your stage.
  2. Budget fit: published prices range from $3,000 to six figures, so shortlist agencies you can actually afford.
  3. Scalability: make sure the identity is a system, with guidelines and files your team can use without the agency.
  4. Who does the work: ask whether you’ll work with senior designers or be handed to a junior team.
  5. Timeline: check that the agency can deliver before your raise, launch or demo day.

Questions to ask before signing

Send each shortlisted team the same brief, including your audience, launch date, budget and the decisions you still need to make.

  • Which deliverables are included: positioning, messaging, identity, website design, development and launch support?
  • Who will lead the work, and can you see a comparable project with their specific role explained?
  • What research, feedback rounds, milestones and client decisions are included in the schedule?
  • Who owns the final files, and are fonts, photography, development or licensing billed separately?
  • What happens if the scope changes, and what will your team need to maintain the identity after handoff?

Compare the scope behind each quote, since a visual identity, strategy engagement and website build are different purchases.

For a starting point on scope, ownership and third-party materials, review the AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services and ask a qualified adviser about your own contract.

Which agencies specialize in tech startup branding?

From this list, Bolder focuses on deep tech such as AI, robotics, biotech and energy.

The Branx focuses on AI and SaaS startups, and Second Eight on science, health and AI companies.

Ramotion and Clay combine branding with product and web design.

If you’re still researching, see my articles on tech startup logos, SaaS logos and the brand strategy framework for startups.

Which startup branding agencies also design websites?

Most startups need the identity and the website at the same time, so check this before you shortlist.

  • Bolder prices early-stage branding and websites together, from $15,000.
  • Second Eight designs and develops websites in the brand, and designs product UI.
  • Ramotion and Clay lead with web and product design alongside the brand.
  • Mucho lists websites next to identity, packaging and environments.
  • The Branx: ask for a quote that covers both the identity and the website.
  • Ebaqdesign adds a week of website design in Figma and one or two weeks of development in Framer, Webflow or Next.js.

Ask who builds the site, which platform it runs on, and who can edit it after launch.

Best logo design agencies for early-stage startups

At pre-seed or seed, you usually need a credible logo and identity system quickly, not a six-month brand program.

Bolder lists early-stage work from $15,000, while Ebaq Design is a solo option at $3,000 for one week; ask The Branx for a current quote.

If speed matters most, you can also compare 13 branding agencies that deliver in one week.

Pricing considerations

Bolder and Ebaq Design publish starting prices, while the figures for The Branx and Motto below come from Clutch. Other firms provide quotes on request.

  • Solo branding expert: $3,000 per week, from one week for an identity (Ebaqdesign).
  • Startup-focused studios: Bolder starts at $15,000 for pre-seed and seed projects; Clutch lists The Branx at $25,000+ but also shows a $20,000 package, so ask the agency to clarify.
  • Second Eight: a weekly rate, with the number of weeks agreed before the project starts.
  • Established agencies: $35,000–$200,000 for full brand building (Bolder’s Series A to IPO range).
  • Motto: Clutch lists a $100,000+ minimum project size; confirm current scope and pricing directly.

For a detailed breakdown of logo budgets, see how much a logo costs.

If you already have a brand, see how much a startup rebrand costs by provider.

A useful identity can help a startup present itself consistently, but it cannot guarantee investment, sales or that a later rebrand will be unnecessary.

faq.question: What is the best branding agency for startups?
faq.answer: It depends on your stage, budget and product. Bolder and The Branx focus on early-stage tech, Second Eight on science, health and AI startups, Ramotion and Clay on brand plus product design, and Motto or Further on larger positioning work. A solo senior designer such as Ebaqdesign suits a focused identity on a tight timeline.

faq.question: How much does a startup branding agency cost?
faq.answer: Published reference points range from $3,000 per week with a solo senior designer, to $15,000 for early-stage work at Bolder, to $35,000–$200,000 for Series A-to-IPO programs. Clutch lists Motto at a $100,000+ minimum. Many agencies quote per project.

faq.question: How long does startup branding take?
faq.answer: From one week for a focused identity, to about three weeks for The Branx process, two to eight weeks for early-stage work at Bolder, and 16 weeks or more for a fast-track startup project at Motto.

faq.question: Do startup branding agencies also design websites?
faq.answer: Many do. Bolder, Second Eight, Ramotion, Clay, Mucho and Ebaqdesign all design websites alongside the identity; ask who builds the site and which platform it uses before you sign.
